The main Apple report explicitly records `native-flutter-driver` with exit 0
and `passed=true`, alongside successful install, launch, VM discovery and
termination. This is simulator evidence, not a physical-device result. Safari's
original complete journey also passed inside the separate input job, including
both trusted clipboard clicks; its later input failure remains a failure.

## Browser input layers

All four framework targets failed their primary-keyboard-focus precondition
before text injection. Verified cleanup allowed the independent trusted W3C
targets to run in fresh sessions. Both results remain in each suite summary.

| Browser | Last reported W3C stage / issued actions | What was **not** issued |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Chrome | `prompt-type`; prompt pointer click and initial text key actions | Shift+Enter; the driver timed out waiting for the `shift-enter` stage. |
| Edge | `prompt-type`; prompt pointer click and initial text key actions | Shift+Enter; the driver timed out waiting for the `shift-enter` stage. |
| Firefox | Through `model-escape`; initial text, Shift+Enter, second line, model open and Escape | Keyboard copy; the driver timed out waiting for `keyboard-copy`. |
| Safari | Through `keyboard-copy`; additionally select-all/copy and its acknowledgement | Clear/delete; the driver timed out waiting for `keyboard-clear`. |

A timeout waiting for the next stage does not show that the next action failed.
These driver reports did not preserve the application's original terminal
integration error. That observation gap requires a subsequent fix and run; no
underlying input failure is inferred from an unissued action.

## AT capability and pilot

Narrator's compiled fixture, native accessibility, ordinary Tab/Space response
and Narrator process were observed. The Windows runner had no default WASAPI
render endpoint (`0x80070490`, Element not found); no utterance or audio was
accepted. The fixture event log also changes from beta to alpha without phase
timestamps, so beta focus at the Narrator command and the cause of that change
are not established. Running audio services alone did not establish an endpoint.

The Catalog pilot's runner metadata and build provenance both identify the exact
commit above. Its GTK preflight received the real Basic Where Am I handler, but
the polled diagnostic file did not expose the subsequent `SPEECH OUTPUT` line.
Separate Speech Dispatcher events and nonzero PCM continued; they do not verify
the spoken words. Cleanup was verified. The Catalog process was never started
and all three task command lists remained empty. A later PTY capture fix does
not retroactively change this result.

Application-wide AT acceptance and human review remain `not_accepted` for both
the capability probes and this pilot.

## Integrity and attribution

[87299572-ci.json](./87299572-ci.json) stores every run and job ID, 18 finalized
artifact IDs, upload-action ZIP SHA-256 values, downloaded-content manifest
hashes, and hashes of the core reports. ZIP digests come from the exact GitHub
upload logs; independently hashed extracted files are identified separately.
The pilot's own artifact manifest was also verified against all 13 files.

Full downloaded artifacts, job logs and per-artifact content manifests were
retained under `/tmp/beautiful-ci-87299572` during collection. GitHub artifacts
may expire according to their retention policy; this committed record retains
the exact IDs and integrity values without embedding large logs or audio.
